Privacy Policy

Last updated: May 6, 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Ampstowatt.com collects, uses, stores, shares, and protects information when you visit our website, use our electrical calculators, read our educational content, contact us, or interact with advertising and analytics technologies. If you do not agree with this Privacy Policy, please discontinue use of the website.

Privacy Policy Contents

  • Cookies and similar technologies

  • Contact us

1. Information We Collect

Information you provide directly

We may collect information that you voluntarily provide when you contact us, such as your name if included, email address, message content, support request details, correction request, privacy request, or any information you choose to include in an email.

Information collected automatically

When you visit the website, our hosting, security, analytics, and advertising technologies may automatically process limited technical information, such as IP address, browser type, device type, operating system, referring URL, pages visited, approximate location derived from IP address, date/time of access, error logs, and interaction data.

Calculator inputs

Calculator inputs such as amps, volts, power factor, wattage, hours, distance, or conductor selections are processed in your browser for the purpose of showing results. We do not require account registration to use the calculators.

2. How We Use Information

  • To operate, maintain, secure, and improve Ampstowatt.com.
  • To provide calculators, reference content, and educational explanations.
  • To respond to support requests, privacy requests, and content correction reports.
  • To detect abuse, spam, security incidents, invalid traffic, or technical problems.
  • To understand website performance, page popularity, and user experience trends.
  • To display, measure, and improve advertising where advertising services are enabled.
  • To comply with legal obligations, enforce our Terms, and protect user safety.

3. Google AdSense and Advertising Disclosure

Ampstowatt.com may display advertisements through Google AdSense or other advertising partners. Google and its partners may use cookies, web beacons, IP addresses, device identifiers, browser information, ad interaction data, and similar technologies to serve ads, measure ad performance, prevent fraud and abuse, limit how often an ad is shown, and personalize ads where permitted.

Google’s use of advertising cookies enables it and its partners to serve ads based on visits to this website and/or other websites. Users may manage ad personalization through Google’s ad settings and learn more about Google advertising technologies at Google Advertising Technologies.

We do not encourage users to click advertisements, we do not compensate users for ad clicks, and we do not place ads in a way intended to mislead users. Ad placements, if active, are intended to comply with Google Publisher Policies and provide a clear separation between website content and advertisements.

4. Cookies and Similar Technologies

Cookies are small files stored on your browser or device. Ampstowatt.com and third-party services may use cookies or similar technologies for essential functionality, security, analytics, advertising, consent management, fraud prevention, and preference storage.

For users in regions where consent is required, including the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland, we intend to request consent for cookies or local storage and for personalized advertising where required by law and Google policy. If Google advertising services are enabled, we may use a Google-certified Consent Management Platform where required.

For detailed cookie categories and choices, please read our Cookie Policy and Cookie Preferences page.

5. How Information May Be Shared

  • Service providers: Hosting, security, analytics, email, and technical providers may process information to help operate the site.
  • Advertising partners: If ads are enabled, Google and advertising partners may process information as described in this policy and their own policies.
  • Legal compliance: We may disclose information if required by law, legal process, fraud prevention, security investigation, or to protect rights and safety.
  • Business transfers: If the website is transferred, merged, or reorganized, relevant information may be transferred as part of that transaction, subject to this policy or equivalent protections.

We do not sell personal information for money. We also do not require users to create accounts to access the calculators.

6. Data Retention

We retain information only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this policy, such as responding to emails, maintaining security logs, improving the website, complying with legal obligations, or resolving disputes. Technical logs may be retained for a limited period and then deleted or anonymized where practical.

7. Your Privacy Rights and Choices

Depending on your location, you may have privacy rights under laws such as GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, or other applicable regulations. These rights may include access, correction, deletion, portability, restriction, objection, withdrawal of consent, and the right to opt out of certain data uses.

  • You can disable or delete cookies in your browser settings.
  • You can manage Google ad personalization through Google’s advertising controls.
  • You can contact us at ampstowatt@gmail.com or +1 (518) 763-2159 for privacy requests.
  • You can avoid providing optional information by not emailing us or by limiting details in your message.

8. Children’s Privacy

Ampstowatt.com is intended for a general audience and educational use. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 or the applicable age of digital consent in a user’s jurisdiction. If you believe a child provided personal information, please contact us so we can review and delete it where appropriate.

9. International Users

Users may access Ampstowatt.com from different countries. Data may be processed in countries with privacy laws different from your own. Where required, we rely on appropriate safeguards, consent, contractual protections, or other lawful mechanisms for international data processing.

10. Security

We use reasonable technical and organizational measures designed to protect information from unauthorized access, misuse, alteration, or loss. No website, email system, or internet transmission is completely secure, so users should avoid sending sensitive electrical plans, financial data, passwords, or confidential personal information by email.

11. Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect changes in law, website features, advertising services, analytics tools, or operational practices. The “Last updated” date shows the most recent revision. Continued use of the site after an update means you accept the revised policy.

12. Contact Us

For privacy questions or requests, email ampstowatt@gmail.com or call +1 (518) 763-2159. Please include “Privacy Request” in the subject line when making a rights request.

Methodology, Review Notes, and Sources

How this calculator works

The calculator applies Watt's law for DC and resistive loads, then adds power factor for AC loads and the 1.732 multiplier for balanced three-phase line-to-line calculations.

  • DC and resistive loads: W = A x V
  • Single-phase AC: W = A x V x PF
  • Three-phase AC: W = 1.732 x A x V x PF

Editorial review

Last reviewed: June 26, 2026. Ampstowatt.com is built around the amps to watts conversion — our core specialty. Content is maintained by the Ampstowatt editorial team and checked for formula consistency, unit labels, calculator behavior, and safety wording.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Fast answers for the amps to watts formula, common conversions, and safe planning limits.

W How do I convert amps to watts?

Multiply amps by volts to get watts. For example, 10 amps at 120 volts equals 1,200 watts (10 × 120 = 1,200). For AC circuits with motors or compressors, also multiply by the power factor from the equipment nameplate.

AC What is the formula for amps to watts?

There are three formulas depending on the circuit type. DC: Watts = Amps × Volts. AC single-phase: Watts = Amps × Volts × Power Factor. AC three-phase (line-to-line): Watts = 1.732 × Amps × Volts × Power Factor. For three-phase line-to-neutral: Watts = 3 × Amps × Volts × Power Factor.

1A How many watts are in 1 amp?

1 amp equals a different number of watts depending on the voltage. At 12V, 1 amp = 12 watts. At 120V, 1 amp = 120 watts. At 240V, 1 amp = 240 watts. This assumes power factor of 1.00. For AC motor loads with lower power factor, the real watts will be lower.

V Do I need voltage to convert amps to watts?

Yes — you cannot convert amps to watts without knowing the voltage. Amps measure current flow, and watts measure power. The relationship is Watts = Amps × Volts. Without voltage, there is no way to determine how much power the current represents. A 10-amp load could be 120 watts (at 12V) or 2,400 watts (at 240V).

PF Why does AC amps to watts need power factor?

Power factor (PF) measures how efficiently a device uses current. Resistive loads like heaters use all the current for real work (PF = 1.0). Motors and compressors draw extra current due to inductance, so their power factor is lower (0.70–0.95). Without accounting for PF, you would overestimate watts by 10–40% for these loads.

VS What is the difference between amps and watts?

Amps (amperes) measure the flow rate of electric current — how much charge passes a point per second. Watts measure electric power — the rate at which electrical energy is used or converted to heat, light, or motion. You need both amps and volts to calculate watts: Watts = Amps × Volts.

3P How do I convert three-phase amps to watts?

For three-phase with line-to-line voltage: Watts = √3 × Amps × Volts × Power Factor (√3 ≈ 1.732). For line-to-neutral voltage: Watts = 3 × Amps × Volts × PF. Example: 10A at 480V with PF 0.90 using line-to-line voltage = 1.732 × 10 × 480 × 0.90 = 7,478 watts.

Wh Is watts the same as watt-hours?

No. Watts (W) measure instantaneous power — how fast energy is being used right now. Watt-hours (Wh) measure total energy consumed over time. A 100-watt light bulb running for 3 hours uses 300 watt-hours (0.3 kWh). Your electricity bill charges per kilowatt-hour, not per watt.

APP Can I use this calculator for appliances?

Yes. Enter the amperage from the appliance nameplate, the outlet voltage (120V or 240V in the US), and power factor if listed. For resistive appliances (heaters, toasters, hair dryers), use PF = 1.0. For motor-driven appliances (refrigerators, AC units, washing machines), use the nameplate PF or estimate 0.85.

SA Can I use this calculator for breaker or wire sizing?

You can use the result for load planning, but not for final breaker or wire sizing. The NEC requires that continuous loads (3+ hours) stay at or below 80% of the breaker rating. Final sizing must account for wire gauge, ambient temperature, conduit fill, voltage drop, and local code. Always consult a licensed electrician for safety-critical work.
